source_signature.text:
theorem exists_selectedAtomicCyclicIsometry
    (family : RepresentativeShellFamily)
    {K : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℂ K]
    [CompleteSpace K] (sigma : Representation Limit K)
    (eta : MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.GNSClass Limit → K)
    (heta : ∀ i, ‖eta i‖ = 1)
    (hstate : ∀ i, Representation.vectorFunctional sigma (eta i) =
      (MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.representative completedRootPureState i).1) :
    ∃ W : MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState →ₗᵢ[ℂ] K,
      (∀ i x, W (MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.selectedEmbedding completedRootPureState i x) ∈
        Representation.cyclicSubspace sigma (eta i)) ∧
      (∀ i, W (MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.selectedEmbedding completedRootPureState i
        (MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.selectedVector completedRootPureState i)) = eta i) ∧
      (∀ i x, commonFixedProjection
        (fun n ↦ sigma (transportedFlag family i n)) (W x) ∈
          ℂ ∙ eta i) ∧
      ∀ a,
        W.toContinuousLinearMap.comp
            (selectedAtomicRepresentation a) =
          (sigma a).comp
            W.toContinuousLinearMap

content.assumptions:
Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra, the completion of the matrix stages $M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ under $a\mapsto a\otimes I_2$. Let $f_n$ be the image of the first diagonal matrix unit, so $f_0=1$ and $f_n$ decreases through projections. The root state $\omega$ takes the value $a_{00}$ on each matrix stage.

Choose one pure state $\varphi_j$ from each unitary-equivalence class $j\in I$ of pure-state Gelfand-Naimark-Segal (GNS) representations, with root index $o$ and $\varphi_o=\omega$. Write $(H_j,\pi_j,\xi_j)$ for its complete complex GNS space, unital star representation and unit cyclic vector. Set $\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{j\in I}H_j$, $\pi=\bigoplus_j\pi_j$, and let $e_j:H_j\to \mathcal H$ be the coordinate embedding. No countability of $I$ is assumed. Inner products are linear in the second argument.

A supplied shell family consists of unital complex star automorphisms $\alpha_j$ and elements $w_{j,n}\in A$. Put $f_{j,n}=\alpha_j(f_n)$. The identities are $\varphi_j\circ\alpha_j=\omega$, $w_{j,n}^*w_{j,n}=f_{j,n}-f_{j,n+1}$ and $w_{j,n}w_{j,n}^*=f_n-f_{n+1}$. At the root, $\alpha_o$ is the identity and $w_{o,n}=f_n-f_{n+1}$. The family is an input, not an existence conclusion. The vectors $\eta_j$ are given simultaneously, one for each chosen class. No irreducibility of $\sigma$ and no density of any individual orbit in all of $K$ is assumed. The algebra and the representations are unital, so each $\eta_j$ belongs to $M_j$.
content.conclusion: The isometry identifies the atomic Hilbert sum with a closed subspace reducing $\sigma$. Each ambient limiting flag projection sends this range into the indicated cyclic line. This is control on the isometry range; it is not a claim that the entire ambient fixed space has dimension one.
content.display_title: Assembling selected GNS cyclic subspaces into an isometric source representation
content.lean_realization_notes: Surjectivity is not part of this theorem. [The surjective cyclic-sum theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/CaptureRange.lean#L32-L261) proves it in the generated-target setting with additional hypotheses. The present hypotheses already supply the vector states; they do not assert that every representation of the CAR algebra contains all selected classes.
content.natural_language_statement:
For the shell family and selected GNS spaces below, let $\sigma:A\to B(K)$ be a unital complex star representation on a complete complex Hilbert space. Suppose unit vectors $\eta_j\in K$ satisfy $\langle\eta_j,\sigma(a)\eta_j\rangle=\varphi_j(a)$ for every $j\in I$ and $a\in A$. Put $M_j=\overline{\{\sigma(a)\eta_j:a\in A\}}$ and let $P_j$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\bigcap_n\operatorname{ran}\sigma(f_{j,n})$.

There is a complex-linear isometry $W:\mathcal H\to K$ such that $W(e_jH_j)\subseteq M_j$, $W(e_j\xi_j)=\eta_j$ and $P_jW x\in\mathbb C\eta_j$ for every $j$ and $x\in \mathcal H$. For every $a\in A$, it satisfies $W\pi(a)=\sigma(a)W$.
content.one_sentence_role: Joins mutually orthogonal pure-state cyclic copies and controls the limiting flag projections on their sum.

proof_steps.text: On $M_j$, the restricted representation has the unit cyclic vector $\eta_j$ with pure state $\varphi_j$, and is irreducible. Equality of vector states gives a unitary $U_j:H_j\to M_j$ sending $\xi_j$ to $\eta_j$ and intertwining $\pi_j$ with the restriction of $\sigma$. It extends the orbit map $\pi_j(a)\xi_j\mapsto\sigma(a)\eta_j$.

For $i\ne j$, the orthogonal projection from $M_j$ to $M_i$ intertwines their restrictions, since the cyclic subspaces reduce $\sigma$. A nonzero such intertwiner between irreducible representations would give a unitary equivalence by Schur's lemma, contradicting the distinct selected GNS classes. Thus $M_i\perp M_j$. The maps $U_j$, followed by inclusion into $K$, form an orthogonal family of isometries.

For a fixed $i$, the state identity gives $\varphi_i(f_{i,n})=1$, hence $\sigma(f_{i,n})\eta_i=\eta_i$. Norm compression implies $P_i\sigma(a)P_i=\varphi_i(a)P_i$, so $P_i\sigma(a)\eta_i=\varphi_i(a)\eta_i$. Density of the orbit and closedness of the line give $P_iM_i\subseteq\mathbb C\eta_i$. If $x\in M_j$ with $j\ne i$ and $P_i x\ne0$, normalizing $P_i x$ yields a vector with state $\varphi_i$. Its cyclic space is orthogonal to $M_j$. Then $\langle P_i x,x\rangle=\|P_i x\|^2=0$, a contradiction. Hence $P_iM_j=0$.

For $x=(x_j)\in \mathcal H$, define $W x=\sum_j U_jx_j$, with each summand viewed in $K$. Orthogonality makes this an unconditionally norm-convergent Hilbert sum and gives $\|Wx\|^2=\sum_j\|x_j\|^2$. The coordinate formulas give $W(e_j\xi_j)=\eta_j$. Applying the bounded operator $P_i$ kills every summand except the $i$-th, whose image lies in $\mathbb C\eta_i$. Applying the bounded operator $\sigma(a)$ termwise gives $W\pi(a)=\sigma(a)W$.

content.proof_summary: Identify each cyclic restriction with its selected GNS representation by [pointed cyclic transport](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/CyclicCapture.lean#L26-L107). [Orthogonality of inequivalent cyclic pieces](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/CyclicCapture.lean#L109-L207) allows these identifications to extend to the arbitrary-index Hilbert sum. The [own-piece compression identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/CyclicCapture.lean#L209-L254) and [vanishing on other cyclic pieces](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/CyclicCapture.lean#L256-L305) give the projection assertion; continuity passes the source intertwining law through the convergent sum.

guide: Here `Limit` is $A$, `completedRootPureState` is the root state $\omega$ bundled with its purity proof, and `SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState` is $\mathcal H$. `selectedEmbedding ... i` is $e_j$, `selectedVector ... i` is $\xi_j$, and `eta i` is $\eta_j$, with source index `i` corresponding to the mathematical index $j$. `cyclicSubspace sigma (eta i)` is $M_j$ and `commonFixedProjection` is $P_j$. The arrow `→ₗᵢ[ℂ]` asserts a complex-linear isometry; it does not assert surjectivity. `W.toContinuousLinearMap` is the same map used in the operator identity.
